declared_deviations.why: spec §3 recomputes after every registration and the vendored P0 Harness does exactly that inside each registration event, but it exposes no public Adj emitter; the import writes through the registration API only and never forges a log line, so the terminal adjudication is the state after the last event

declared_deviations.what: imported FCL problem records use SpawnTrigger.SEED
declared_deviations.why: the vendored enum has no 'import' member; 'seed' is the only trigger that does not assert an in-graph derivation. The clean fix is an enum addition, requested rather than papered over

declared_deviations.what: research problems use SpawnTrigger.RESEARCH with empty criteria
declared_deviations.why: the vendored enum has the member and §12 is exactly this path, but the trigger is not part of the v1.3 enum text; criteria stay empty because no instantiated commitment id is a criterion

declared_deviations.what: document-local depends refs are dropped, not turned into dep edges
declared_deviations.why: at node granularity they would be dep self-loops, i.e. cycles; toposort rejects them and a self-loop asserts nothing the author declared

declared_deviations.what: a self-targeting objection mints no warrant
declared_deviations.why: a Dung self-attack means 'this argument is self-defeating', which is not what an intra-document caveat asserts; minting it would flip two labels for reasons that have nothing to do with the evidence

declared_deviations.what: an objection against a record this import reified as a warrant attacks that warrant's validity node, not the node artifact
declared_deviations.why: spec §1 closure: attackers of a validity node attack the warrant and every carrier of it, so criticism of a criticism keeps its force instead of collapsing into a plain edge onto the carrier

declared_deviations.what: the retargeting rule above has ONE exception: an objection against a criticism carried by the SAME artifact is not retargeted
declared_deviations.why: the §1 closure lifts an attack on a validity node onto every carrier of the warrant, and for an intra-document criticism of a criticism that carrier is the objector itself, so retargeting would mint a self-attack through the closure and make the artifact self-defeating - which is not what an author asserts by qualifying their own earlier objection. `objection.o4` against `o1`/`o2` is exactly this case; it is dropped, not retargeted, and counted under its own code so the loss is visible rather than silent

declared_deviations.what: an FCL `claim` record maps to no spec construct
declared_deviations.why: a claim asserts content without proposing a test, so it is neither an observation-valued commitment nor a criticism nor a problem; it survives in the artifact body and in the FCL-1 document artifact, and is reported here because `uptake_refs_unmapped` covers only the claims the author put in `uptake`

problems.description: I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

Why the one friend avoids the conversations is undetermined: the talks may have become aversive recycling of unwinnable 'what did we mean' disputes, or the avoidance may concern the friendship or life outside the flat, with chores merely where it surfaces. The exposed material cannot distinguish these readings, and a response should not assume either.

Whether the underlying issue is distributive — one person in fact doing much more — or the avoidance is about the friendship rather than the chores cannot be determined from the exposed material. If either holds, better coordination will not touch it, and the honest next move is a different conversation, at a calm moment unrelated to any dispute, about proportion of load or about the friendship itself.

Under unstable schedules the allocation principle itself — equal task counts, weighting by time at home, or by capacity — is unsettled; the trial should treat the principle as revisable at each check-in rather than settled at the outset.

Whether the friend's avoidance tracks the cost of the conversations (the account's operating assumption) or their content is undetermined by the material. o4 and o5 presuppose the content-based possibility without establishing it; the friend's response, or non-response, to any offered format would only partially discriminate between the readings.

Calibration of my own criticism: o1's supporting generalisation — that pure coordination failure produces irritation and workarounds rather than topic-avoidance — is unverifiable from here. If it is false, sustained unwinnable memory-disputes may be aversive enough to produce avoidance on their own, o1 loses its abductive edge and reduces to the weaker but still standing claim that the exclusivity of the account's framing is unearned.

The exposed facts cannot decide whether the friction is about coordination volume or about standing and fairness between the three friends. The structure trial is a diagnostic as much as a treatment — here this account and the selected account converge from opposite sides — and if friction persists after negotiation is removed, the needed conversation is one no coordination system can substitute for.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#r5): Stop adjudicating past ambiguous agreements and declare a clean slate for future ones: what a past loose agreement meant cannot be reconstructed, only superseded.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#r6): Move future chore agreements onto one shared, persistent medium — whiteboard, shared note, or app — where each entry names task, owner, deadline, and a one-line done-criterion, offered as a two-week trial.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#r7): Build schedule-change into the system with a standing rule: a schedule change that blocks a claimed task triggers a say-so by an agreed day and a re-deal.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#r8): Re-approach the avoidant friend at a cost level they may accept: ask which format they would actually tolerate — a ten-minute time-boxed check-in or asynchronous messages — and offer the trial in that form, framed as convenience rather than accountability. Ask; do not diagnose.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/rival#r5): Propose, at a calm moment and framed as a preference question rather than a negotiation, a fixed trial of about one month of a structure that needs no per-task agreement: either whole domains owned outright with autonomy over how and when, or a fixed rotation that runs by default.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/rival#r6): For the avoidant friend, offer participation at near-zero conversational cost: a domain or rotation slot chosen by preference where possible, swappable by message, with the single question 'which would you hate least' instead of a renegotiation.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/rival#r7): Do one rough workload check when domains or the rotation are first allocated, then leave the allocation untouched until the trial ends.
